text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text. This training data includes books, websites, and articles from the internet. When you give an LLM a prompt, the way you write it matters a lot; this is called prompt engineering. LLMs can answer questions, translate languages, and write texts. However, they sometimes make mistakes or give wrong information, because they do not truly understand meaning like humans do.
